clue.text: A Parisienne occupied by a struggle in the dark

indicators.note: a place occupied by something has it inside, so the French article holds the next pieces

parts.note: a Parisian woman would say une for 'a', the French feminine article
war is a struggle between armed sides

explanation.surface: A Paris woman finds herself caught up in a fight with the lights out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Parisienne' looks like a woman but means the French feminine article, what a Parisienne says for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone kept in the dark is uninformed, ignorant of what is going on.

clue.text: Regular habit

explanation.surface: A monk's everyday robe.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular means consistent or the same throughout, and a habit is a standard outfit worn by all members of an order.

clue.text: A number came into line when spoken to

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
soldiers dress ranks when they line up straight on parade

explanation.surface: A squad of soldiers falls in when a sergeant barks at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' is a drill term: troops dress when they straighten their line.
explanation.definitionFit: To address someone is to speak directly to them, so spoken to is the participle sense.

clue.text: Endow a section of a hospital

parts.note: a ward is a room or department for patients in a hospital

explanation.surface: A benefactor funds a hospital wing.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give or grant something formally, as a prize is granted.

clue.text: Winning over the listener in the finish

indicators.note: one piece sits within another, so the hearing organ goes inside the word for the close

parts.note: an ending is a finish
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A speaker wins the audience round at the close of the speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is only a link; 'Winning' is the adjective, as in a winning smile, not the act of victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning as an adjective means charming or appealing, as in a winning smile.

clue.text: The serving man found a buyer that's right

parts.note: something sold has found someone to buy it
i.e., Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A footman or servant managed to sell something and was correct to do so.
explanation.definitionFit: A man serving in the army is a private in the forces, a fighting man.

clue.text: Stain spoiling beautiful material

indicators.note: something spoiling is going to ruin, so the letters of the first word are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A mark that ruins a lovely fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth glossy fabric, prized for its sheen.

clue.text: Such guides take English money as well as German

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the sign for the British pound
and means as well as
the mark was Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Tour guides being paid in pounds and marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is a link; 'German' supplies money only because 'money' covers it too.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark is a prominent feature that travellers use to find their way.

clue.text: Put down, though the really cold weather hasn't begun

indicators.note: something that has not begun is missing its start, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: winter is the season of the coldest weather

explanation.surface: A burial goes ahead before the deep frost sets in.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, putting a body down in the ground.

clue.text: A feature showing admiration

explanation.surface: One quality of a person that inspires esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: A respect is a particular point or aspect, as in 'in this respect', and respect also means esteem or regard.

clue.text: In the country, some speak in dialect

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run within them

explanation.surface: In rural parts some locals talk in a regional accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the country' reads as 'rural', but 'the country' is the definition, a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation of South Asia.

clue.text: Eminent backer, meeting a setback, blows up!

indicators.note: read as one who goes back, the word for eminent is written backwards

parts.note: an eminent person is noted, well known
read as A plus the word set put back, giving the letters TES

explanation.surface: A prominent financial supporter suffers a reverse and explodes in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backer' and 'setback' both pose as finance words but are reversal signals: NOTED backwards is DETON, and A plus SET backwards is ATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that detonates explodes.

clue.text: Being in debt, vendor possibly accepts 26

indicators.note: a word that accepts another takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other
possibly signals the letters of the seller's word may be arranged another way

parts.note: 26 across is a word meaning naive or inexperienced, and raw means the same

explanation.surface: A seller in the red takes on a naive customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles the seller's word, and 'accepts' takes a synonym of the answer to 26 across, not that answer itself, inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdrawn account has had more taken out than was in it, leaving its holder owing the bank.

clue.text: Ruin by north-eastern river

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil or ruin it
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: Devastation beside a river in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marne is a river in north-eastern France, scene of two World War I battles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marne is a French river that joins the Seine near Paris.

clue.text: "What passion cannot — raise and quell?" (Dryden)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Dryden's Song for St Cecilia's Day, praising the art that can stir and calm every feeling

explanation.surface: A line of poetry asking what can both arouse and subdue any emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from John Dryden's A Song for St Cecilia's Day (1687); St Cecilia is the patron saint of the art in question.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryden's ode credits the art of sound and melody with stirring and calming every emotion.

clue.text: Mock suffering, so it's said, for the widow

indicators.note: so it's said tells us the words are spoken, the sound standing for a different spelling

parts.note: mock means sham and suffering means pain, said together

explanation.surface: A bereaved woman is accused of putting on her grief.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAM PAIN said aloud sounds like the answer. 'The Widow' is a nickname for Veuve Clicquot, the famous French sparkling wine house (veuve is French for widow).
explanation.definitionFit: Veuve Clicquot, 'the widow' in French, is a famous brand of sparkling wine from Reims.

clue.text: The consequence to a social worker is grave

parts.note: import means significance or consequence, as in a matter of great import
an ant is a social insect and the worker caste does the labour

explanation.surface: The outcome for someone in social services is serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a care professional, but it is an ant, a colony-dwelling insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave matter is serious and weighty, which is to say significant.

clue.text: The manifest strain of providing music in church

parts.note: manifest means obvious, which is what plain means
a strain is a tune or melody, a song

explanation.surface: An obvious tune forms part of the church's musical offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like effort, but here it is a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is unaccompanied medieval chant, as in Gregorian chant, sung in church services.

clue.text: Men at work on the exterior of some flat

indicators.note: one piece sits outside another, enclosing it
work as an anagram signal means the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: part means some of something

explanation.surface: Builders working on the outside of a block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges MEN AT into A...MENT, which goes 'on the exterior of' PART, the word for 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a set of rooms on one floor of a building, the American word for a flat.

clue.text: Angry head chopped up shrub

indicators.note: chopped up suggests cutting into pieces and reassembling, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A furious gardener hacks back a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrangea is a flowering garden bush with large round flower heads.

clue.text: A player with pluck

parts.note: pluck suggests courage, but this musician plucks strings for a living

explanation.definitionFit: A harpist plays the harp by plucking its strings.

clue.text: The way to offer support must be settled

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way or road
to aid is to give help or support

explanation.surface: The right way to help others needs to be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid means sedate and steady, settled in one's ways.

clue.text: Newspaper leader raised freedom of movement, causing upset

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted upwards, so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the person who leads a newspaper
range is the scope or room to move about

explanation.surface: An editor campaigns for free movement and causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like an editorial column but is the editor himself; 'raised' turns ED upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder or disturb, just as to upset can be.

clue.text: New university involved in strike came second

indicators.note: involved in means placed within, so these letters go inside the word for hit

parts.note: a rap is a sharp blow or strike

explanation.surface: A fresh university gets caught up in industrial action and is runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests a walkout, but here it is a blow, RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up is to finish as runner-up, taking the place just behind the winner.

clue.text: Stricter maybe, but more likeable

explanation.surface: A tougher teacher who is also friendlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice can mean precise or exacting, as in a nice distinction, and also pleasant or agreeable, so both comparatives fit.

clue.text: Fellow found about to reverse in town

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a college at Oxford or Cambridge
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

indicators.note: to reverse means to turn backwards, so the short word for concerning is read the other way

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A college fellow discovered he was about to back down in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' reads as 'discovered', but it is the verb to found metal, to CAST it. DONCASTER is a town in South Yorkshire, famous for horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doncaster is a town in South Yorkshire, England, home of the St Leger horse race.

clue.text: A tendency to pile up

explanation.surface: A habit of accumulating things.
explanation.definitionFit: A drift is a general trend or tendency, and snow or sand drifts when wind heaps it up.

clue.text: Article and note on royal letters giving rise to strong feeling

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
G is a musical note
ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A letter written with a royal seal causes a powerful emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing G before ER in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is a powerful emotion of rage or displeasure.

clue.text: New title, it's falsely assumed

parts.note: a fresh name taken on falsely, as a celebrity travelling under another identity does

explanation.definitionFit: Travelling incognito means doing so under a false name to hide who one is.

clue.text: Concerned about the environment, but easily fooled

explanation.surface: An eco-activist who falls for every trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Green describes ecological politics, and also a naive novice who is gullible.

clue.text: Ambiguous term not occasioning distress

indicators.note: something ambiguous can be read in more ways than one, so the letters are open to rearrangement

explanation.surface: A vague word that causes no upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' looks like a negative in the surface, but it is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe suffering, great anguish.

clue.text: Put an end to a restrictive application

explanation.surface: Stopping something with a limiting use.
explanation.definitionFit: To garotte is to kill by strangling, ending a life, and the garotte is a cord pulled tight round the throat.
